title: Two-Year Outcomes of the Paul Glaucoma Implant for Treatment of Glaucoma

license.statement: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article <license>); non-commercial no-derivatives, therefore private

indication: refractory glaucoma uncontrolled on maximal tolerated medical therapy, with or without previous failed glaucoma surgery: POAG 19, PACG 11, neovascular 4 and other secondary or juvenile glaucoma 11 eyes; 11 eyes with previous trabeculectomy or tube; ages 21-80 years; retrospective single-center review including patients of a prospective interventional study (Singapore)

groups.description: PAUL Glaucoma Implant (non-valved), plate under the recti 9 mm from the limbus, pericardial patch, 'stability system' with cross-linked viscoelastic beneath the patch; no mitomycin C, ligature or intraluminal stent; 28 eyes had combined phacoemulsification and 6 another concurrent procedure; 45 eyes of 45 patients

series.baseline_label: Table 2 'Mean intraocular pressure (mm Hg)' block, row 'Preoperative' = mean medicated preoperative IOP (same cell text as Table 1 'Mean medicated intraocular pressure', T1!R11C2)
series.notes: mean ± SD (column header 'Data (Mean±SD)'); rows Preoperative, 1 mo, 6 mo, 12 mo, 18 mo, 24 mo; follow-up cells carry a significance asterisk (not used); no patient was lost to follow-up and none needed additional glaucoma surgery or explantation, so no eye was censored (Results)

notes: Reference kind 'preoperative_medicated': the tabulated preoperative IOP is the mean medicated preoperative IOP; all patients were on IOP-lowering medications (mean classes in Table 1 R21).
Tonometer: Goldmann applanation, two readings averaged (third if they differed by > 2 mmHg), method 'goldmann'.

The cohort mixes PGI alone and PGI combined with phacoemulsification (28 of 45) or other concurrent procedures (6 of 45); no per-subgroup IOP is tabulated, so the whole cohort is extracted with procedure 'tube' (the drainage device defines the arm).

Slit-lamp procedures (laser suture lysis, iridoplasty, needling, anterior chamber viscoelastic injection) were not counted as reoperations; four eyes had viscoelastic injection for hypotony and four tube occlusions were treated (standard postoperative management).
Number of classes of IOP-lowering medications preoperatively and at 12/18/24 months is tabulated in Table 2 (not extracted).
